skill.name: release
skill.description: Guides release creation for a monorepo with prefixed Git tags, version bumps, branch sync, and GitHub Release workflows.
skill.summary: Guides tag-based plugin releases for the Codename-11 Stash Downloader monorepo.
skill.author: Codename-11

security_audit.summary: The skill contains many Markdown command examples; most backtick and URL hits are false positives or legitimate release commands. Confirmed risks are npm, git, and remote push operations in the release workflow, especially tag deletion and branch publishing. No prompt injection text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Remote release commands lack a final confirmation gate.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit maintainer approval before git push, tag deletion, tag creation, or GitHub release actions.

remediation.issue: Release commands mix read-only checks with write operations.
remediation.suggestion: Separate verification, local mutation, and remote publishing steps, and require branch, remote, and version checks before each write step.

remediation.issue: The secret reference could be misread as agent-managed configuration.
remediation.suggestion: State that GOOGLE_API_KEY is managed only by GitHub Actions and must not be read, printed, or copied by the agent.

content.value_statement: Manual plugin releases can miss version, tag, and deployment steps. This skill guides branch checks, version bumps, prefixed tags, GitHub Actions checks, and GitHub Release creation.
actual_capabilities: Identifies whether Stash Downloader or Stash Browser should be released.
Checks branch state, uncommitted changes, type checks, lint, tests, and builds before release.
Guides version bump selection from commit history and package version.
Creates prefixed Git tags for downloader and browser plugin releases.
Coordinates main and dev branch synchronization around GitHub Actions deployments.
Documents recovery steps for cancelled stable deployments.
limitations: Designed for the Codename-11 Stash Downloader monorepo, not general repositories.
Requires Git, npm, GitHub remote access, and permission to push release branches or tags.
Does not replace human review of version numbers, changelogs, or release notes.
Can trigger CI and publishing side effects when commands are executed.

use_cases.title: Ship a plugin update
use_cases.description: Follow a repeatable release path for Stash Downloader or Stash Browser after development is complete.

use_cases.title: Coordinate tag-based deployment
use_cases.description: Use prefixed tags and GitHub Actions timing rules to avoid cancelled stable deployments.

use_cases.title: Prepare a release PR
use_cases.description: Create a reviewable release branch for larger changes before merging, tagging, and publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Check Release Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the release skill to inspect the current branch, working tree, tests, lint, and build status for Stash Downloader. Report any blockers before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Version Bump
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the release skill to compare commits since the latest downloader tag and recommend patch, minor, or major. Do not push anything yet.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Browser Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the release skill to update Stash Browser for a patch release, commit the version bump, and show the exact tag plan for approval.

prompt_templates.title: Recover a Cancelled Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the release skill for a downloader release after a cancelled deployment. Verify the workflow state, propose the safest tag recovery, and ask before any remote push.

output_examples.input: Release readiness check for Stash Downloader.
output_examples.output: The report lists the current branch, working tree status, check results, current version, latest matching tag, and release blockers.

output_examples.input: Plan the next Stash Browser release.
output_examples.output: The response recommends a version bump, explains the commit evidence, names the prefixed tag, and waits for approval before publishing.
The assistant identifies the cancelled workflow, explains tag recovery risk, and asks for confirmation before deleting or re-pushing tags.

best_practices: Confirm the plugin, target version, branch, and remote before any write operation.
Run checks before version bumps, tags, or GitHub release actions.
Wait for the stable workflow to finish before syncing dev.
anti_patterns: Do not run release commands in a repository that has not been verified.
Do not push main, dev, or tags without explicit maintainer approval.
Do not expose environment variables or API keys while reviewing release automation.

faq.question: Which repositories is this for?
faq.answer: It is for the Codename-11 Stash Downloader monorepo and its downloader and browser plugins.

faq.question: Does it create GitHub Releases directly?
faq.answer: It guides tag and branch steps that trigger GitHub Actions, which creates the release when configured.

faq.question: Can it choose the version bump?
faq.answer: It can recommend a bump from commit history, but a maintainer should approve the final version.

faq.question: Does it need network access?
faq.answer: Remote pushes and GitHub checks require network access through Git and GitHub tools.

faq.question: Does it handle cancelled deployments?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents tag recovery and branch sync steps, but those steps require confirmation.

faq.question: Is it safe for automatic execution?
faq.answer: No. It can change branches, create tags, and push to remotes, so humans should confirm publishing actions.
